mainTopic: How חכמים can cancel debts through שביעית today (הפקר בית דין הפקר), and the standing of הלל's פרוסבול
overview: The גמרא explains that today, by תורה law, שביעית does not cancel debts. חכמים made it cancel them anyway as a reminder, and הלל then made the פרוסבול. The גמרא asks how חכמים can cancel a debt the תורה says is owed. אביי answers that they only tell the borrower to stay passive (שב ואל תעשה). רבא answers that הפקר בית דין הפקר, which is proven from פסוקים in עזרא and יהושע. Next the גמרא asks whether הלל made פרוסבול only for his own generation or for all generations. Two proofs from שמואל are both pushed away, and רב נחמן says he would strengthen פרוסבול so that even an unwritten one counts. A side discussion explains שמואל's word עולבנא as insolence and praises people who are insulted but do not answer back. Finally, רב חסדא begins to explain the word פרוסבול, and the explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: חכמים made שמיטה cancel debts, and הלל made the פרוסבול
steps.stepSummary: This finishes the earlier answer. By תורה law, שביעית today does not cancel debts. חכמים still made it cancel debts as a reminder, and when people stopped lending, הלל made the פרוסבול.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the rabbis set up that שביעית should cancel debts anyway, as a reminder of the real שביעית. הלל saw that people stopped lending to each other, so he stood up and set up the פרוסבול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an answer it began earlier: in our times, debt-cancellation by שביעית is only a rabbinic rule, so הלל's פרוסבול did not go against the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the question was how הלל could stop a תורה law from working. The answer is that today the cancellation is only דרבנן, so הלל was only adjusting a rabbinic rule. This sets up the next question: how could the rabbis cancel a debt the תורה says is still owed?

keyTerms.meaning: The rabbis set up (made a new rule)
It will cancel (debts)
A reminder of the שביעית year
A document handing one's debts to בית דין so שביעית does not cancel them

phrases.english: And the rabbis set up that it should cancel [debts],
phrases.notes: "It" means the שביעית year, which today by תורה law would not cancel debts.

phrases.english: as a reminder of the Shemitah year;
Hillel saw that the people held back
from lending to one another,
so he stood up and set up the prosbol.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes an answer that started before this section, explaining that debt-cancellation today is only דרבנן.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reclassifying the law: today's cancellation of debts is only rabbinic, so הלל's fix does not clash with the תורה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: הלל seemed to be uprooting a תורה law by making the פרוסבול.
steps.terutzMaskana: Today the cancellation is only a rabbinic reminder, so הלל was only adjusting a rabbinic rule.

steps.title: How can the rabbis cancel a debt the תורה says is still owed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that חכמים made שביעית cancel debts when the תורה does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: But is there such a thing, where by תורה law שביעית does not cancel the debt, and the rabbis set up that it does cancel it?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from step 1. If the תורה says the borrower still owes the money, how can חכמים tell him he doesn't have to pay?
steps.deeperAnalysis: By תורה law the lender still owns the money he is owed. A rabbinic rule canceling the debt looks like the rabbis letting the borrower keep someone else's money. So the question is: where do חכמים get that power?

keyTerms.meaning: Is there really such a thing? (a challenge)
By תורה law
Cancels (debts)

phrases.english: But is there such a thing
where by Torah law Shemitah does not cancel [the debt],
and the rabbis set up that it should cancel it?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אִיכָּא מִידֵּי דְּמִדְּאוֹרָיְיתָא לָא מְשַׁמְּטָא שְׁבִיעִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rabbinic rule described in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that חכמים made שביעית cancel debts today.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If by תורה law the debt is still owed, a rabbinic rule canceling it seems to take money away from its rightful owner.

steps.title: אביי: The rabbis only tell the borrower to stay passive
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the rabbis are not taking money. They are only telling the borrower to sit back and not pay, which is שב ואל תעשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: It is a case of "sit and do not act."
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives the first answer: the rabbinic rule only asks the borrower to do nothing, meaning not pay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חכמים have the power to tell a person not to do something, even when that leaves a תורה duty unfulfilled, as long as no active step is taken. Here the borrower simply does not pay, so חכמים are only telling him to stay passive. On this view the money is still owed by תורה law; the rabbis just tell him not to pay it.

keyTerms.meaning: Sit and do not act: being passive, not doing anything

steps.confusionAlert: אביי does not say the debt is truly gone. He only says the rabbis may tell the borrower not to act. That is exactly where רבא will differ.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
It is "sit and do not act."
phrases.notes: The borrower is told just not to pay. He isn't told to do anything active.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: שֵׁב וְאַל תַּעֲשֶׂה הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits what the rabbis are doing: they are only telling the borrower to be passive.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rabbis seemed to be actively taking the lender's money away.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rabbis only tell the borrower not to pay, and they may do that even against a תורה duty.

steps.title: רבא: בית דין can declare property ownerless
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a different answer: בית דין has the power to make property ownerless, so the rabbis can really cancel the debt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: What בית דין declares ownerless is ownerless.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the same question in a new way: בית דין truly has power over people's money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבא it is not only that the borrower stays passive. בית דין can actually take ownership away, so the debt is really canceled. This is a stronger power than אביי's.

keyTerms.meaning: What the court declares ownerless becomes ownerless
Ownerless property

steps.whyThisMatters: הפקר בית דין הפקר is a basic rule all over the גמרא: it gives חכמים real power over money matters.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Property the court declares ownerless is ownerless.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: הֶפְקֵר בֵּית דִּין הֶפְקֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the קשיא of step 2, different from אביי's.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the court real power over money, so the debt is truly canceled.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only the תורה can make a debt stop being owed.
steps.terutzMaskana: בית דין can take ownership away, so the rabbis' cancellation really works.

steps.title: רבי יצחק's source from the פסוק in עזרא
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק proves הפקר בית דין הפקר from a פסוק in עזרא: whoever did not come when the leaders said would lose all his property.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי יצחק said: From where do we know that what בית דין declares ownerless is ownerless? As it says: "And whoever does not come within three days, by the order of the officers and the elders, all his property will be forfeited, and he will be separated from the community of the exile."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק to back up רבא's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the time of עזרא, the leaders ordered that anyone who did not show up within three days would lose all his property. This shows that the leaders, the court, could take away a person's possessions. That is the source for בית דין's power over money.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know?
All his property will be forfeited
The officers and the elders (the leaders)

phrases.english: As Rabbi Yitzchak said:
From where do we know that what the court declares ownerless is ownerless?
As it says:
"And whoever does not come
within three days
by the order of the officers and the elders,
all his property will be forfeited
and he will be separated from the community of the exile."

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: מִנַּיִן שֶׁהֶפְקֵר בֵּית דִּין הֶפְקֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for רבא's rule in step 4.
steps.raayaObject: The rule הפקר בית דין הפקר.
steps.raayaSupportSource: עזרא 10:8, where the leaders took away the property of anyone who did not come.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר's source: the leaders who divided the land
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר brings a different source, a פסוק in יהושע listing the leaders who gave out the portions of ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר said, from here: "These are the inheritances that אלעזר the כהן, and יהושע bin נון, and the heads of the fathers, etc., gave out."
steps.whatsHappening: A second source for הפקר בית דין הפקר begins. The גמרא quotes the פסוק first and will explain it in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר points to the wording "heads of the fathers" in the list of those who divided the land. The proof itself comes from explaining that phrase, which is what the next two steps do.

keyTerms.meaning: From here (a different source)
Inheritances, portions of land
The heads of the fathers (the family leaders)

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer said, from here:
"These are the inheritances that were given out by
Elazar the Kohen and Yehoshua bin Nun
and the heads of the fathers, etc."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different פסוק as the source for the same rule proven in step 5.
steps.raayaObject: The rule הפקר בית דין הפקר.
steps.raayaSupportSource: יהושע 19:51, about the leaders who divided ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: Why does the verse link "heads" with "fathers"?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the פסוק puts the word "heads" (leaders) together with "fathers."
steps.simpleTranslation: What do "heads" have to do with "fathers"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out an odd phrase in the פסוק, setting up the explanation that will give the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Leaders and fathers seem like different things, so why join them in one phrase? This question opens the way to compare the two.

keyTerms.meaning: What does one thing have to do with the other?

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי מָה עִנְיַן רָאשִׁים אֵצֶל אָבוֹת?
phrases.english: And what do "heads" have to do with "fathers"?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי מָה עִנְיַן רָאשִׁים אֵצֶל אָבוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks closely at the wording of the פסוק quoted in step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the פסוק puts the word "heads" together with "fathers."

steps.title: Leaders can give out property like fathers do
steps.stepSummary: The answer: just as fathers can give their children whatever they want, leaders can give the people whatever they want, which proves בית דין's power over property.
steps.simpleTranslation: To teach you: just as fathers can give their children an inheritance of whatever they want, so too leaders can give the people whatever they want.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the link between "heads" and "fathers", and this completes רבי אליעזר's proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A father may decide how to give out his own property to his children. The פסוק compares the leaders to fathers, teaching that leaders can also take and give out property as they decide. So בית דין can move money from one person to another, and the rabbis can cancel debts.

keyTerms.meaning: To teach you
Give as an inheritance, hand out property
Whatever they want

steps.whatToRemember: Two answers to how the rabbis can cancel a debt the תורה says is owed: אביי says it is only שב ואל תעשה (the borrower just doesn't pay). רבא says הפקר בית דין הפקר, meaning the court really can take ownership away. That power is proven from עזרא (רבי יצחק) or from the leaders who divided the land, who are compared to fathers (רבי אליעזר).

phrases.english: To teach you:
just as fathers give an inheritance to their children
of whatever they want,
so too leaders give the people
whatever they want.

steps.triggerLanguage: לוֹמַר לָךְ: מָה אָבוֹת מַנְחִילִין אֶת בְּנֵיהֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7 and completes רבי אליעזר's proof.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק compares leaders to fathers: just as fathers give out their property as they wish, leaders can give out property to the people as they wish.

steps.title: Was the פרוסבול enactment for one generation or for all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises a question: did הלל make פרוסבול only for his own generation, or for all future generations too?
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: when הלל made the פרוסבול, did he make it only for the people of his time, or also for all generations?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question, an איבעיא, about how far הלל's enactment of פרוסבול reaches. It wants to know whether it was meant only for his time or forever.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Either way, people still use פרוסבול. The question is about where its authority comes from: is it still standing on הלל's own enactment, or is it only something later generations kept doing?

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among the Sages (a real open question, not an attack)
A document that hands a loan over to בית דין so שמיטה does not cancel it
He made a rabbinic enactment (תקנה)
For his own generation
For all generations

phrases.english: A question was asked of them:
When Hillel instituted the prosbol,
was it for his own generation that he instituted it,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא לְדָרֵי עָלְמָא נָמֵי תַּקֵּין?
phrases.english: or perhaps he instituted it for all generations too?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question about פרוסבול after the discussion of הפקר בית דין.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether הלל's enactment of פרוסבול was for his generation only or for all generations.

steps.title: What difference does it make?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference the question makes, since פרוסבול is used either way.
steps.simpleTranslation: What difference does it make?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to ask why the question matters at all. This sets up the next step, which explains the practical difference.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since people keep writing פרוסבול in both cases, the question looks like it changes nothing. The גמרא wants a real practical result before going on.

keyTerms.meaning: What practical difference does it make?

phrases.english: What practical difference does it make?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the practical point of the question in step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical result that depends on the answer to step 9.

steps.title: The difference: whether a later court can cancel it
steps.stepSummary: If פרוסבול was only for הלל's generation, a later court can cancel it. If it was for all generations, only a greater court could cancel it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference is about cancelling it. If he made it only for his generation, we can cancel it. But if he made it for all generations, a court cannot cancel what another court decided unless it is greater in wisdom and in number. So what is the answer?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the difference is whether a later בית דין is allowed to cancel פרוסבול. Then it asks again: so which is it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a rule that one בית דין cannot cancel another בית דין's enactment unless it is greater in wisdom and in number. If הלל's enactment still stands for all generations, nobody today could cancel it, since no court is greater than הלל's. If it was only for his time, there is no enactment left to protect, so it can be dropped.

keyTerms.meaning: To cancel it

keyTerms.term: אֵין בֵּית דִּין יָכוֹל לְבַטֵּל דִּבְרֵי בֵּית דִּין חֲבֵרוֹ
keyTerms.meaning: A court cannot cancel the decision of another court
Greater than it in wisdom and in number
What is it? (So what is the answer?)

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a basic rule of rabbinic law: an enactment made by an earlier court is protected. Only a greater court may undo it.

phrases.english: For cancelling it.
If you say it was for his own generation that he instituted it,
we can cancel it;

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ לְדָרֵי עָלְמָא נָמֵי תַּקֵּין,
phrases.english: but if you say he instituted it for all generations too,

phrases.aramaic: הָא אֵין בֵּית דִּין יָכוֹל לְבַטֵּל
phrases.english: then a court cannot cancel
the decision of another court,
unless it is greater than it
in wisdom and in number.
So what is the answer?
phrases.notes: The גמרא is asking again: so which is it, for his generation or for all generations?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 10 by giving the practical result, then repeats the question from step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The difference is whether a later court may cancel פרוסבול, since a court cannot cancel another court's enactment unless it is greater in wisdom and in number.

steps.title: Proof from שמואל: a פרוסבול is written only in סורא or נהרדעא
steps.stepSummary: שמואל said a פרוסבול may be written only in the courts of סורא or נהרדעא. If הלל's enactment stood for all generations, any court should be able to write one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: שמואל said, we write a פרוסבול only in the court of סורא or the court of נהרדעא. If you think הלל made it for all generations, then let other courts write it too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to answer the question from step 9 with a statement of שמואל. The proof points toward 'only for his generation.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: If הלל's enactment still stood for all generations, it would be enough on its own, and any ordinary court could write a פרוסבול. Since שמואל limits it to the two great courts, it seems the power today comes from those strong courts themselves, not from הלל's enactment.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear (an attempt to prove something from a source)
We do not write
Court (בית דין)
And if it enters your mind (if you think)

phrases.english: Come and hear, for Shmuel said:
We do not write a prosbol
except either in the court of Sura
or in the court of Nehardea.
And if it enters your mind
that he instituted it for all generations too,
then let them write it in other courts too!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to settle the question repeated at the end of step 11.
steps.raayaObject: That הלל made פרוסבול only for his own generation.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל's ruling that a פרוסבול is written only in the courts of סורא and נהרדעא.

steps.title: Rejection: for all generations, but only for strong courts
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed away. הלל may have made it for all generations, but only for courts as powerful as his own or like רב אמי and רב אסי, which can take away money.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps when הלל made it for all generations, he made it only for courts like his own, and like רב אמי and רב אסי, who are strong enough to take money away. But for all other courts, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from שמואל. Limiting פרוסבול to great courts fits even if הלל made it for all generations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof assumed that 'for all generations' means 'for every court.' The rejection splits the two: the enactment may last forever but only work in courts strong enough to take money from people, like סורא and נהרדעא. So שמואל's rule does not answer the question, and it stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps (often used to push away a proof)
They are strong (have strong authority)
To take away money from someone's ownership
Two great אמוראים who led an important court

steps.whatToRemember: The question of whether פרוסבול was for הלל's generation or for all generations is not settled here. שמואל's rule that only great courts write a פרוסבול fits both sides.
steps.confusionAlert: 'For all generations' does not have to mean 'for every court.' The גמרא shows an enactment can last forever and still work only in very powerful courts.

phrases.aramaic: דִּלְמָא כִּי תַּקֵּין הִלֵּל לְדָרֵי עָלְמָא –
phrases.english: Perhaps when Hillel instituted it for all generations,
it was for courts like his own court,
and like Rav Ami and Rav Asi,
who are strong enough to take money away;
but for everyone else, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּלְמָא כִּי תַּקֵּין הִלֵּל לְדָרֵי עָלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 12.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from שמואל's statement.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed that an enactment for all generations must be usable by every court. It may have been for all generations but only for courts powerful enough to take away money.

steps.title: שמואל says he would cancel פרוסבול if he could
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a new proof: שמואל called פרוסבול an עולבנא of the judges and said he would cancel it if his strength grew.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: שמואל said, 'This פרוסבול is an עולבנא of the judges. If my strength grows, I will cancel it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries again to answer the question from Step 9. It quotes שמואל, who said he would cancel פרוסבול if he had more power.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If שמואל thought he could cancel פרוסבול, it seems הלל made it only for his own generation. Otherwise a later court like שמואל's would have no power to undo it.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear: the גמרא is bringing a source as a proof
פרוסבול, the document that keeps a loan from being cancelled by שמיטה
A word whose meaning the גמרא will ask about (insolence or convenience)
Judges
If my strength grows (if I gain more power)

phrases.english: Come and hear, for Shmuel said:
This prosbol is an ulbena of the judges;
phrases.notes: Leave עולבנא untranslated for now. The גמרא will soon ask exactly what this word means.

phrases.english: if my strength increases, I will cancel it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the earlier proof was pushed away in Step 13, the גמרא tries a new proof from another statement of שמואל.
steps.raayaObject: That הלל made פרוסבול only for his own generation
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל's statement that he would cancel פרוסבול if his strength grew

steps.title: How can שמואל cancel it? A court must be greater to undo another court's rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how שמואל could cancel it, since a court can cancel another court's rule only if it is greater in wisdom and in number.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'I will cancel it'?! But a court cannot cancel the words of another court unless it is greater than it in wisdom and in number!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is surprised that שמואל could talk about cancelling הלל's enactment. This sharpens the proof: it seems שמואל must hold that פרוסבול was only for הלל's generation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The known rule is that a later court can undo an earlier court's rule only if it is greater. שמואל was not greater than הלל. So, the argument goes, he could only cancel it if הלל never made it for all generations.

keyTerms.meaning: A court cannot cancel
Another court (literally, its fellow court)
Greater than it
In wisdom and in number (of judges or students)

phrases.english: 'I will cancel it'?!
But isn't it so that a court cannot
cancel the words of another court,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן גָּדוֹל הֵימֶנּוּ בְּחָכְמָה וּבְמִנְיָן!
phrases.english: unless it is greater than it in wisdom and in number!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבַטְּלִינֵּיהּ?! וְהָא אֵין בֵּית דִּין יָכוֹל לְבַטֵּל דִּבְרֵי בֵּית דִּין חֲבֵרוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions שמואל's statement, and by doing so makes the proof stronger.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's claim that he could cancel פרוסבול
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A court may not cancel another court's enactment unless it is greater. So שמואל's words only make sense if הלל's פרוסבול was never meant for all generations.

steps.title: שמואל meant: only if I become greater than הלל
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed away. שמואל meant he would cancel פרוסבול only if he became greater than הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he meant: if my strength grows so that I am greater than הלל, I will cancel it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof by explaining שמואל's words differently. He was speaking about a time when he might be greater than הלל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With this reading, שמואל's statement fits the rule that only a greater court can cancel. So it does not prove that פרוסבול was only for הלל's generation. The question from Step 9 stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he meant (the גמרא re-explains someone's words)
More than הלל

phrases.english: This is what he said: if my strength increases
more than Hillel's, I will cancel it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָאָמַר: אִם אֲיַישֵּׁר חַיִל יוֹתֵר מֵהִלֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from Steps 14-15 by reading שמואל's words more narrowly.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only this proof. It does not decide the question either way.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed שמואל meant he could cancel פרוסבול as he was. Really he meant only if he became greater than הלל.
steps.whatToRemember: No proof has settled whether הלל made פרוסבול for all generations. שמואל's words fit either side.

steps.title: רב נחמן says he would uphold פרוסבול
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן takes the opposite stance: if his strength grew, he would uphold פרוסבול.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב נחמן said: I would uphold it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא contrasts רב נחמן with שמואל. Instead of cancelling פרוסבול, רב נחמן says he would strengthen it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל was uncomfortable with פרוסבול, while רב נחמן liked it. His exact meaning is not clear yet, and the גמרא will ask about it next.

keyTerms.meaning: I will uphold it, I will make it stand

phrases.english: And Rav Naḥman said: I will uphold it.
phrases.notes: He means he'd uphold it if his strength increased, the same condition שמואל used.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an opinion opposite to שמואל's in Step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב נחמן wanted to strengthen פרוסבול, not cancel it.

steps.title: פרוסבול is already in force
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what 'uphold' means, since פרוסבול is already in force.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'I will uphold it'?! It is already upheld and standing!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב נחמן's wording. What is there to uphold if פרוסבול already works?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Upholding something only makes sense if it is weak or in danger. Since פרוסבול is already fully in use, 'I will uphold it' seems to add nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: It is already upheld and standing

phrases.english: 'I will uphold it'?!
But it is already upheld and standing!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the wording of רב נחמן's statement.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: You cannot uphold something that is already fully in force.

steps.title: Even an unwritten פרוסבול would count as written
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן meant he would add a new rule: even without a written פרוסבול, it counts as if one were written.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he meant: I will say something new about it, that even if a פרוסבול was not written, it is treated as if it was written.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'uphold' means 'strengthen even more.' רב נחמן would make every loan protected, even without a written document.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Right now a lender must actually write a פרוסבול. רב נחמן would remove that need, so every debt would act as if a פרוסבול existed. That is a real addition to הלל's enactment.

keyTerms.meaning: I will say something about it (add a new rule)
Even though
It is treated as if written

phrases.english: This is what he said: I will say something about it,
that even though it was not written,
it is considered as if it was written.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 18.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Uphold' seemed pointless, since פרוסבול already works.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Uphold' means strengthening it, so that an unwritten פרוסבול counts as written.
steps.whatToRemember: שמואל would weaken פרוסבול if he could. רב נחמן would strengthen it so that it works even without writing.

steps.title: What does עולבנא mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether שמואל's word עולבנא means insolence or convenience.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: this word עולבנא, does it mean insolence, or does it mean convenience?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to שמואל's word from Step 14 and asks what it means. This sets up the next step, which brings a source to answer it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If it means insolence, שמואל felt פרוסבול lets lenders boldly collect money that שמיטה should have cancelled. If it means convenience, the judges were making things easier for themselves.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised among them
A word meaning insolence or boldness
A word meaning convenience or ease

phrases.english: A dilemma was raised before them:
Is this ulbena a term of insolence,
or is it a term of convenience?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to a word in שמואל's statement from Step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the word עולבנא

steps.title: עולא's bride who sinned under her canopy
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings עולא's saying, which uses the same root, עלובה, to mean insolent. That shows the word means insolence.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: עולא said, 'Insolent is the bride who sinned under her own wedding canopy.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by showing the same root used elsewhere. In עולא's saying it clearly means shameless or insolent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A bride who betrays her husband at her own wedding is the height of boldness. Since עולא called her עלובה, the root means insolence, and so does שמואל's עולבנא.

keyTerms.meaning: Insolent, shameless (same root as עולבנא)
Bride
Wedding canopy

phrases.english: Come and hear, for Ulla said:
Insolent is the bride
phrases.notes: עולא is describing the Jewish people, who sinned with the עגל right after receiving the תורה.

phrases.english: who was promiscuous under her own wedding canopy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 20 with a parallel use of the word.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: עולבנא means insolence, as in עולא's עלובה כלה.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two meanings. Here עלובה means shameless, not 'poor' or 'pitiful.'

steps.title: The פסוק behind עולא's saying
steps.stepSummary: רב מרי gives the פסוק that hints at עולא's idea: 'While the king was at his table, my spikenard gave off its scent.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מרי, the son of שמואל's daughter, said: What is the פסוק? 'While the king was at his table, my spikenard gave off its scent.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב מרי shows where עולא's idea comes from in תנ״ך. The king was still celebrating when the bride's perfume gave off its smell.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The king at his table stands for ה׳ at the giving of the תורה. The scent given off at that very moment hints at the sin of the עגל, the bride's betrayal right at the wedding.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the פסוק (the source)?
At his table, at his celebration
My spikenard, a type of perfume

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב מָרִי בְּרַהּ דְּבַת שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Rav Mari, son of Shmuel's daughter, said:
What is the verse?
"While the king was at his table,
my spikenard gave off its scent."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב מָרִי בְּרַהּ דְּבַת שְׁמוּאֵל: מַאי קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק behind עולא's saying in Step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עולא's idea comes from the פסוק 'While the king was at his table, my spikenard gave off its scent.'

steps.title: ה׳'s affection still remains
steps.stepSummary: רבא notes that the פסוק says 'gave off its scent' and not 'reeked.' This shows ה׳ still loves us.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: His affection is still with us, since it is written 'gave off,' and it is not written 'reeked.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds a comforting point. Even when describing the sin, the פסוק uses gentle words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק could have said the perfume stank. It chose the soft wording 'gave off its scent' instead. That shows ה׳'s love for us lasted even after the עגל.

keyTerms.meaning: Affection, love
With us
It reeked, it stank

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא: עֲדַיִין חַבִּיבוּתָא הוּא גַּבַּן,
phrases.english: Rava said: The affection is still with us,
as it is written "gave off,"
and it is not written "reeked."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: עֲדַיִין חַבִּיבוּתָא הוּא גַּבַּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a positive lesson from the wording of the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The gentle wording of the פסוק shows that ה׳'s affection for us remains.
steps.whatToRemember: עולבנא means insolence, as in עולא's 'insolent bride.' Even so, the פסוק's soft wording shows ה׳ still loves us.

steps.title: Praise for those who are insulted but do not insult back
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that people who are insulted but stay quiet, and who accept suffering with love, are compared to the rising sun in its strength.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: People who are insulted but do not insult others, who hear themselves shamed but do not answer back, who serve out of love and are happy even when they suffer, are the ones the פסוק describes: 'Those who love Him are like the sun going out in its strength.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that uses the same root, עלב (insult), and praises people who take insults without fighting back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא brings this ברייתא because it uses the same root, עלב, as עולבנא and עלובה, here in the form נעלבין, people who are insulted. It praises someone who is insulted and stays silent. This is a side lesson on the same root, not another answer to the question of step 20.

keyTerms.meaning: people who are insulted
insulting others
their shame or disgrace
suffering, hardships
the Rabbis taught (introduces a ברייתא)

steps.whatToRemember: The root עלב means insult. Someone who is insulted and does not answer back is compared to the powerful rising sun.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
Those who are insulted but do not insult others,
who hear their shame but do not answer back,
who act out of love and are happy in their suffering,
about them the verse says:
"And those who love Him are like the sun going out in its strength."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the side discussion about the root עלב, adding a ברייתא that praises silently accepting insult.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: People who are insulted but do not insult back, and who accept suffering with love, are compared to the sun rising in its strength.

steps.title: What does the word פרוסבול mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to its main topic and asks for the meaning of the word פרוסבול.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does the word 'פרוסבול' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The side discussion is over, and the גמרא returns to פרוסבול and asks what the word itself means. This sets up רב חסדא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the סוגיא talked about the law of פרוסבול, the document that lets a lender collect debts after שמיטה. Now the question is only about the word. It is not a challenge, just a request for a definition.

keyTerms.meaning: the document הלל enacted so a lender can collect debts after שמיטה
what is?

phrases.english: What is the meaning of "prosbol"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side discussion about עלב and returns to the main subject of פרוסבול.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the word פרוסבול.

steps.title: רב חסדא explains the word פרוסבול
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says פרוסבול means 'an enactment for בולי and בוטי.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: It means an enactment (פרוס) for בולי and בוטי.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the question by splitting the word: פרוס means an enactment, made for the בולי and the בוטי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads the one word פרוסבול as a short form of a longer phrase. The first part, פרוס, means an enactment or decree. The words בולי and בוטי are two groups the enactment is for, and the גמרא will explain them in the next lines.

keyTerms.meaning: an enactment or decree
one group of people the enactment helps (the גמרא explains this next)
a second group the enactment helps (the גמרא explains this next)

steps.confusionAlert: פרוסבול is not two separate Hebrew words. רב חסדא is explaining a foreign word by breaking it into parts.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
An enactment for bulei and butei.
phrases.notes: Hold on for what בולי and בוטי mean; the גמרא explains them right after this.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: פְּרוֹס בּוּלֵי וּבוּטֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 25 about the meaning of פרוסבול.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: פרוסבול is short for פרוס בולי ובוטי, an enactment for the בולי and the בוטי.
